claim: The paper cites nothing. In thirty-one pages that rewrite the kinematics its contemporaries were arguing about, there is no reference list, no numbered citation, and no footnote pointing to another author's work. It does name people, but only as adjectives attached to theories: the Maxwellsche theory for bodies at rest, the Maxwell-Hertzsche equations, the Lorentzsche theory of the electrodynamics of moving bodies. A reader is told whose theory is meant and never where to find it. Poincaré, Michelson and Morley are not named at all. What the paper does end with is one sentence of thanks: that while he was working on the problem treated here his friend and colleague M. Besso stood loyally by him, and that he owes him several valuable suggestions. Besso was a patent-office colleague rather than a collaborator, and he is the only person the paper names who is not a theory. Read the silence carefully. It is evidence about how the paper presents itself, not evidence about what Einstein had read.
evidence: Three measurements against the records in this repository, 2026-10-08. (1) NO CITATION APPARATUS: the paper's 209 source blocks under content/source-blocks/special-relativity carry exactly seven kinds, closing, equation, footnote, heading, masthead, paragraph and part-heading. There is no block of kind reference. Its four footnotes are s1-fn1 (p. 893, the imprecision in the concept of simultaneity), s2-fn1 (p. 896, what 'Zeit' means here), s4-fn1 (p. 903, defining the rigid sphere) and s6-fn1 (p. 909, a symmetry argument); none cites a work. (2) WHICH NAMES APPEAR: searching the blocks, Maxwell occurs in 8, Hertz in 6, Lorentz in 2, Besso in 1, and Poincaré, Michelson and Morley in none. The three theory names are adjectival, for example 'der Maxwellschen Theorie für ruhende Körper' at s0-p2 and 'der Lorentzschen Theorie der Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper'. My own first draft of this note asserted that Maxwell and Lorentz were absent, which the search refuted before it was committed. (3) THE THANKS TO BESSO: closing-ack holds 'Zum Schlusse bemerke ich, daß mir beim Arbeiten an dem hier behandelten Probleme mein Freund und Kollege M. Besso treu zur Seite stand und daß ich demselben manche wertvolle Anregung verdanke' at printed page 921, with Besso in the emphasis run the plate shows. The transcriptions read here are machine drafts with hand correction rather than a reviewed ledger, which is why this note is reviewState draft. It makes no claim about whom Einstein had actually read, which is a different historical statement needing its own evidence.
